papers.title: Unveiling the mechanism of metabolites derived from gut microbiota in the treatment of acute kidney injury via network pharmacology and bioinformatics.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects a considerable proportion of patients that represents a major challenge for clinical treatment. Gut microbiota metabolites have been reported to attenuate acute kidney injury (AKI), yet their underlying mechanisms remain largely elusive. The present study aimed to explore the protective mechanisms of these metabolites against AKI using.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and bioinformatics to investigate how gut microbiota metabolites protect against acute kidney injury (AKI), aiming to uncover the underlying molecular mechanisms. The findings provide a systems-level view of potential therapeutic targets and pathways, though the abstract is incomplete and lacks specific results.

papers.title: A Critical Synthesis of Machine Learning in Autism Spectrum Disorder Genomic Research: From Transcriptomics to Microbiome.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent impairments in social communication, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors. This narrative review synthesizes advances in machine learning applications to ASD genomic research through May 2026, spanning gene expression analysis, whole-exome sequencing (WES), non-coding variant interpretation, multi-omics integration, single-cell transcriptomics, epigenetic profiling, and gut microbiome analysis. A purposive, thematic literature synthesis approach was employed, allowing broad coverage o
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes recent advances in applying machine learning to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) genomic research, covering transcriptomics, whole-exome sequencing, non-coding variants, multi-omics, single-cell, epigenetics, and microbiome studies. It highlights how ML methods are being used to identify ASD risk genes, interpret variants, and integrate diverse data types, providing a broad overview of the field's progress and challenges.

papers.title: Maternal secretor status and human milk oligosaccharides influence the infant gut resistome.
papers.abstract: The infant gut resistome is established early in life and is shaped by perinatal exposures, yet the mechanisms underlying its modulation remain unclear. We combined shotgun metagenomics of fecal samples from 57 one-month-old infants and paired milk samples from 50 mothers in the MAMI cohort to investigate the influence of maternal secretor status on early-life resistome development. Longitudinal follow-up at 6 and 12 months, and also further validation in the independent Lifelines NEXT (LLNEXT) cohort, support our findings. Cesarean section (C-section) was associated with increased antibiotic
papers.summary: This study investigates how maternal secretor status and human milk oligosaccharides shape the infant gut resistome (collection of antibiotic resistance genes) in early life. Using metagenomic data from the MAMI cohort and validation in an independent cohort, the authors find that C-section delivery is associated with increased antibiotic resistance gene abundance, while maternal secretor status and milk oligosaccharides influence the resistome composition. The findings highlight modifiable maternal factors that could impact infant gut resistome development.

papers.title: Syndromic cholera diagnosis masks diverse causes of diarrhoeal disease in Burundi revealed by portable metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Cholera outbreaks remain a major public-health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, where diagnostic capacity is limited and clinical case definitions are non-specific and re ly heavily on syndromic diagnosis. Rapid identification of Vibrio cholerae is critical, yet cholera-suspected diarrhoea can have multiple infectious causes not captured by targeted diagnostics.
papers.summary: This study used portable metagenomics to analyze diarrheal samples from suspected cholera cases in Burundi, revealing that many cases were caused by pathogens other than Vibrio cholerae, highlighting the limitations of syndromic diagnosis. The findings underscore the need for broader diagnostic approaches to accurately identify etiologies and improve outbreak management.

papers.title: xoxF-linked methanol oxidation signals recur across wetland metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Wetlands are globally important methane-cycling ecosystems, but methanol oxidation remains less frequently emphasized than methane oxidation in community-level metagenomic analyses. Recent studies have highlighted the ecological importance of the lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase XoxF, yet wetland-focused xoxF literature remains comparatively limited relative to marine, freshwater, and other environmental systems. Here, we screened wetland-associated records in IMG/M using methane-metabolism and enzyme-centered queries focused on EC 1.1.2.10/xoxF and related methanol-oxidation annota
papers.summary: This study screens wetland metagenomes from IMG/M for methanol oxidation genes, particularly the lanthanide-dependent xoxF, and finds that xoxF-linked methanol oxidation signals recur across diverse wetland ecosystems. The work highlights the ecological importance of methanol oxidation in wetlands, which is often overshadowed by methane oxidation research, and suggests that xoxF is a widespread and integral part of wetland microbial methane cycling.

papers.title: Rumen DNA virome plasticity and viral metabolic potential are associated with seasonal adaptation in grazing yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
papers.abstract: As a diverse and abundant component of the rumen ecosystem, viruses interact with other microorganisms and are thought to influence microbial metabolism and host productivity. However, how the rumen virome responds to seasonal fluctuations in extreme environments remains poorly understood. Here, metagenomic analyses were used to investigate temporal dynamics of viral diversity, functional potential, and virus-host associations in the rumen virome of yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau across warm and cold seasons.
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to characterize how the rumen virome of grazing yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau changes between warm and cold seasons, revealing seasonal plasticity in viral diversity and metabolic potential. The findings suggest that viruses may play a role in helping these ruminants adapt to extreme environmental fluctuations by influencing microbial metabolism.

papers.title: Decadal Resampling Reveals Widespread Increases in Soil Microbial Diversity Associated With Nitrogen Deposition.
papers.abstract: Simulated manipulation experiments, such as nitrogen addition to mimic atmospheric nitrogen deposition, are widely used in global change research. However, experimental manipulations may differ from real-world environmental change in their intensity, duration, and co-occurrence, leaving long-term changes in soil microbial communities and soil health insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we resampled soils from 38 forest and grassland ecosystems across eastern China in 2009 and 2019 and assessed microbial taxonomic and functional diversity using shotgun metagenomics. Microbial diversi
papers.summary: By resampling soils from 38 forest and grassland sites across eastern China a decade apart, this study found that soil microbial diversity increased broadly over time, and this increase was associated with nitrogen deposition. The findings highlight that real-world environmental changes can have different effects on soil microbial communities than short-term experimental nitrogen additions.

papers.title: Comorbidity Mechanism and Management of Chronic Low Back Pain and Major Depressive Disorder: From Neural Circuit Remodeling to Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: This review systematically elaborates multi-system interactive mechanisms underlying comorbid chronic low back pain (CLBP) and major depressive disorder (MDD), synthesizes recent advances in diagnosis, treatment, and management, and proposes precision medicine directions to address clinical challenges, including missed diagnosis, treatment resistance, and poor prognosis.
papers.summary: This review systematically examines the shared neural circuit and multi-system mechanisms underlying comorbid chronic low back pain and major depressive disorder, and synthesizes recent diagnostic and therapeutic advances. It proposes precision medicine strategies to address clinical challenges such as missed diagnosis and treatment resistance.

papers.title: The Calcidiscus leptoporus genome reveals vitamin-mediated holobiont interactions.
papers.abstract: Coccolithophores are major marine phytoplankton that contribute to ocean carbon cycling through both organic carbon fixation and calcium carbonate biomineralization, yet the functional basis of their interactions with phycosphere bacteria remains poorly resolved. Here, we present the nuclear genome of the haploid phase of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus, a coccolithophore that calcifies in both life-cycle stages. We combined host genome analysis, genome-resolved characterization of associated bacteria, and a four-month vitamin-manipulation experiment to test how B-vitamin biosynthet
papers.summary: This study presents the nuclear genome of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus and combines it with metagenomic and experimental approaches to reveal that interactions with phycosphere bacteria are mediated by B-vitamin exchange, highlighting a vitamin-based holobiont relationship.

papers.title: Metagenome-scale modeling to assess microbiome metabolic complementarity for precision microbiota transplantation therapies.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) holds therapeutic promise beyond recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, but clinical outcomes remain unpredictable and donor-selection strategies remain limited, in part because the role of donor‒recipient metabolic interactions in shaping the post-FMT community remains poorly understood. Here, we leverage metagenome-scale metabolic modeling to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient microbiomes and predict post-FMT community composition. Using MICOM-derived metabolic models, we show that donor genomes whose metabolic f
papers.summary: This study uses metagenome-scale metabolic modeling to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient gut microbiomes, aiming to improve donor selection for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). The authors demonstrate that donor genomes with higher metabolic complementarity to the recipient predict post-FMT community composition more accurately, offering a computational approach to personalize FMT therapies.

papers.title: Longitudinal development of infant oral ecosystem: salivary metabolomic, bacteriome, and virome dynamics in early infancy.
papers.abstract: This prospective cohort study investigated the longitudinal development of the salivary bacteriome, virome, and metabolome during early infancy. We assessed the associations between oral bacteria, viruses, and metabolites from 10 mother-infant dyads, with oral samples collected at 1 and 2 years of age. Forty saliva and plaque samples underwent untargeted metabolomic analysis, and infant saliva samples underwent metagenomic sequencing. Maternal salivary and plaque metabolomic profiles remained largely stable, whereas infant profiles were clearly separated from maternal profiles and changed with
papers.summary: This study tracks how the infant oral ecosystem—including bacteria, viruses, and metabolites—develops between ages 1 and 2, showing that infant profiles are distinct from their mothers and evolve over time. The findings highlight coordinated changes in the salivary microbiome and metabolome during early childhood, offering insights into oral ecosystem maturation.

papers.title: Endophytic bacteria associated with turmeric, ginger and white radish exhibit dual roles as producers of antibacterial metabolites and carriers of multidrug resistance.
papers.abstract: The increasing global burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) necessitates the exploration of unconventional microbial niches for novel bioactive compounds. Simultaneously, it is also necessary to evaluate their role in the dissemination of resistant bacteria through the food chain. Endophytic bacteria inhabiting edible plant tissues represent a largely underexplored interface between environmental microbiota and human exposure. In this exploratory study, endophytic bacteria were isolated from fresh rhizomes of Zingiber officinale (ginger), Curcuma longa (turmeric), and Raphanus sativus (whit
papers.summary: This study isolated endophytic bacteria from turmeric, ginger, and white radish, revealing that these bacteria can both produce antibacterial metabolites and carry multidrug resistance genes. The findings highlight edible plant tissues as an underexplored niche where beneficial bioactive compound producers coexist with potential reservoirs for antimicrobial resistance dissemination through the food chain.

papers.title: Causal relationships between oral-gut microbiome and bone neoplasm-related phenotypes: Insights from bidirectional Mendelian randomization.
papers.abstract: The human oral and gut microbiota are the 4 largest microbial communities in the body and play crucial roles in maintaining homeostasis and influencing disease. Observational studies have suggested links between these microbiota and bone neoplasm-related phenotypes, but establishing causality has been challenging due to confounding factors and reverse causality. We conducted a bidirectional, 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study to investigate evidence consistent with a potential causal association between the saliva and gut microbiota and various bone neoplasm-related phenotypes. Geneti
papers.summary: This study uses bidirectional Mendelian randomization to investigate potential causal links between oral/gut microbiota and bone neoplasm-related phenotypes, addressing confounding and reverse causality limitations of observational studies. The findings suggest evidence for causal associations, though the abstract is incomplete and specific results are not fully detailed.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Mock Communities as Quality Control Materials for Clinical Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables comprehensive detection of a broad spectrum of microorganisms. However, its clinical application faces two major challenges: the development of appropriate microbiome-based biomarkers and the need to ensure the reproducibility and quality of the microbiome analytical workflow. Therefore, we developed four types of bead-based mock communities as standard materials for microbiome analysis and evaluated potential experimental biases arising from nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and validation of four bead-based mock communities designed as quality control materials for clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing. The authors evaluated biases introduced during nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis, providing a standardized resource to improve reproducibility and quality assurance in clinical microbiome workflows.

papers.title: Association between Oral Manifestations and Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease-related Esophageal Diseases: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: This scoping review was conducted to map evidence on associations between oral manifestations and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and its related esophageal diseases, including non-erosive reflux disease, erosive esophagitis, Barrett's esophagus and esophageal adenocarcinoma.
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the evidence linking oral manifestations (such as dental erosion and other oral conditions) with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and its related esophageal diseases, including non-erosive reflux disease, erosive esophagitis, Barrett's esophagus, and esophageal adenocarcinoma. The review likely identifies consistent associations, particularly with dental erosion, and highlights gaps in the literature for future research.

papers.title: Deployable high-fidelity metagenome binning at scale with QuickBin.
papers.abstract: Reconstructing genomes from metagenomic assemblies is foundational to microbiome research, yet binning faces a persistent trade-off between fidelity and throughput. Many high-accuracy methods rely on GPU-intensive workflows, marker-gene postprocessing, or heavy computational resources, limiting reproducible use at scale. Here, we present QuickBin, a CPU-native, marker-free binning algorithm designed to recover near-complete, ultra-low-contamination metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) efficiently. QuickBin pairs a GC-coverage spatial index (BinMap) with an early-exit Oracle cascade of similarit
papers.summary: QuickBin is a new CPU-native, marker-free metagenome binning algorithm that recovers near-complete, ultra-low-contamination genomes efficiently at scale, overcoming the trade-off between fidelity and throughput. It uses a GC-coverage spatial index and an early-exit Oracle cascade to achieve high accuracy without GPU-intensive workflows, making it suitable for reproducible large-scale microbiome studies.

papers.title: Community-driven updates for comprehensive long-read metagenomics and enhanced binning in nf-core/mag v5.
papers.abstract: nf-core/mag is a reproducible Nextflow pipeline for best-practice metagenomic de novo assembly, and binning within the nf-core framework. Here we present a major update that adds support for long-read-only assembly and bin refinement, includes five new binning tools, expands taxonomic classification to viruses and eukaryotes, and improves bin quality evaluation with new tools and latest databases. Through sustained community-driven development spanning seven years and four primary curator teams, nf-core/mag remains actively developed as an open-source workflow for metagenomic analysis, benefit
papers.summary: This paper describes a major update to nf-core/mag, a Nextflow pipeline for metagenomic assembly and binning. The update adds long-read support, five new binning tools, expanded taxonomic classification to viruses and eukaryotes, and improved bin quality evaluation, reflecting sustained community-driven development.

papers.title: Natural Infection of Domestic Dogs with Raccoon Dog and Fox Amdoparvovirus During a Severe Disease Outbreak.
papers.abstract: Raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV) has been reported in raccoon dogs and foxes, but natural infection in domestic dogs has not previously been documented. During March-April 2026, samples from four affected Dobermann dogs from a kennel near Novi Sad, Serbia, were submitted for laboratory investigation. After negative testing for canine adenovirus, canine coronavirus, herpesvirus, parvovirus, distemper virus, influenza A virus, and leptospirosis, metagenomic sequencing was performed on selected tissues, followed by bioinformatic analysis and targeted RFAV PCR screening of additional outb
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study documents the first natural infection of domestic dogs with raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV), identified in Dobermann dogs during a severe disease outbreak in Serbia. The dogs tested negative for common pathogens, but metagenomic sequencing and targeted PCR confirmed RFAV, suggesting a potential new host range for this virus.

papers.title: Coenocline Simulation of Microbiome Samples: A Biologically Mechanistic Framework for Generating Ecologically Realistic Synthetic Datasets to Support Classification Method Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Machine learning and statistical classification methods are widely applied to microbiome data for diagnostic, prognostic, and phenotypic insights. However, the complex, multivariate nature of microbiome communities makes it difficult to assess the relative performance of these methods. Most comparisons rely on a small number of published datasets, without considering their underlying ecological properties or how these properties may, in turn, influence classification performance. We introduced a coenocline-based simulation framework to generate synthetic microbiome datasets that incorporate re
papers.summary: This paper introduces a coenocline-based simulation framework to generate synthetic microbiome datasets that mimic realistic ecological gradients, providing a biologically mechanistic approach for evaluating machine learning classification methods. The framework addresses the lack of ecologically grounded synthetic data in microbiome method comparisons, enabling more robust performance assessments.

papers.title: Fruits, Vegetables, and Legumes: Harnessing the Gut-Kidney Axis in Hypertensive Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Hypertension is the most common comorbidity in chronic kidney disease (CKD), affecting roughly 80-85% of patients overall and an even higher proportion in nondialysis CKD G3-G5. This narrative review examines whether, and under what clinical conditions, fruits, vegetables, and legumes can be used safely in adults with hypertensive CKD, especially nondialysis CKD G3-G5, as well as moderate to severe loss of kidney function, paying close attention to the gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acids, gut-derived uremic toxins, potassium bioavailability, and modifiable clinical risk factors. The clinic
papers.summary: This narrative review evaluates the safety and potential benefits of fruits, vegetables, and legumes in adults with hypertensive chronic kidney disease (CKD), focusing on the gut-kidney axis. It discusses how these foods may modulate gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acids, and uremic toxins, while considering potassium bioavailability and clinical risk factors.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework that uses ESM2 protein embeddings and genomic-neighborhood features to fill gaps in functional annotations of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbial metagenomes. Applied to 21 silage metagenomes, CAAC achieved high classification performance (F1-macro 84.64%) and improved coverage of carbohydrate-active enzyme annotations, enabling better interpretation of microbial metabolic potential.

papers.title: The intestinal microbiota mediates inflammatory responses in heat-stressed pigs via the NOD1/RIP2/NF-κB signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: Intestinal inflammation in pigs is widespread, involving complex pathogens, and is exacerbated by heat stress (HS). This study investigated HS alters gut microbiota to activate NOD1/RIP2/NF-κB signaling and induce intestinal inflammation. Twenty pigs exposed to HS (34 ± 1 °C) were compared to 20 controls (25 ± 3 °C). Tissues and feces were collected at intervals. Ninety germ-free mice were randomly divided into nine groups for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) experiments. Histopathological changes in colonic tissue were observed, and inflammatory factors in peripheral blood were quantifi
papers.summary: This study shows that heat stress in pigs alters the gut microbiota, which in turn activates the NOD1/RIP2/NF-κB signaling pathway to drive intestinal inflammation. Fecal microbiota transplantation experiments in germ-free mice confirmed that the heat-stressed microbiota is sufficient to induce inflammatory responses, highlighting the microbiota's causal role in HS-related intestinal damage.

papers.title: Deciphering microbial community dynamics using cross-sectional data-informed NeuralODE.
papers.abstract: Understanding the ecological mechanisms of host-associated microbial ecosystems typically relies on either cross-sectional or time-series data. Cross-sectional analyses are limited in their ability to assess intervention effects, whereas time-series models require dense and informative sampling that is often impractical.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a NeuralODE-based framework that leverages cross-sectional microbiome data to infer microbial community dynamics, overcoming the limitations of traditional time-series models that require dense sampling. The approach enables the assessment of intervention effects and ecological mechanisms from more readily available cross-sectional data.

papers.title: Computational Genomics for Resistome Characterization: Current Advancements and Future Challenges Under a One Health Perspective.
papers.abstract: The resistome, defined as the complete set of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) present in the microbiota of a given environment, is a critical component for understanding the evolutionary dynamics of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and its impact on human, animal, and environmental health. This review summarizes current methods and technological advances and offers a forward-looking perspective on resistome research. A systematic literature search was conducted. References on short-read and long-read sequencing, amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and multi-omics integration were inclu
papers.summary: This review summarizes current computational methods and technological advances for characterizing the resistome—the collection of antibiotic resistance genes in a microbiome—including short- and long-read sequencing, amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and multi-omics integration. It highlights the importance of these approaches for understanding antimicrobial resistance dynamics across human, animal, and environmental health under a One Health perspective, and discusses future challenges.

papers.title: Wastewater Metagenomic Reanalysis of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Public Datasets from Türkiye (Ankara and Hatay).
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antimicrobial resistance in microbial communities is a global health concern that leads to millions of deaths each year. Many bacterial pathogens have resistance to multiple antibiotics. Domestic wastewater treatment facilities are reservoirs for antibiotic-resistant bacteria and resistance genes. Wastewater-based epidemiology surveillance is crucial for monitoring antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Türkiye has one of the highest levels of antibiotic resistance with a lack of research on resistomes. This study is a focused reanalysis of publicly available wastewater met
papers.summary: This study reanalyzed public wastewater metagenomic datasets from Ankara and Hatay in Türkiye to profile antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), addressing a gap in resistome surveillance for a country with high antibiotic resistance. The findings highlight domestic wastewater treatment facilities as reservoirs of diverse ARGs, underscoring the utility of wastewater-based epidemiology for monitoring resistance in understudied regions.

papers.title: Land-Use and Depth-Dependent Assembly of Soil Microbiomes Shapes Ecological Functions, Interaction Networks, and Phytopathogenic Communities Across Crop and Orchard Systems.
papers.abstract: Soil microorganisms are essential for nutrient cycling, plant productivity, and soil health, yet the relative importance of land-use and soil depth in shaping agricultural microbiomes remains poorly understood. This study investigated soil microbial communities across uncultivated land, alfalfa fields, crop systems (feed corn and sweet corn), and orchard systems (walnut and quince) in the Hajdúnánás region of Hungary using shotgun metagenomic sequencing and soil physicochemical analyses. Microbial alpha diversity showed limited variation among land-use systems but declined significantly with s
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to examine how land-use type and soil depth shape soil microbiomes across agricultural systems in Hungary. It found that while microbial diversity varied little among land-use types, depth had a significant effect, and that land use influenced ecological functions, interaction networks, and the abundance of phytopathogenic communities.

papers.title: Tumor Location and Preoperative Biliary Stenting Shape Gut Microbiome Diversity in Pancreatic Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Recent evidence suggests that gut microbiome plays a role in the development of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and influences treatment response. However, the association of tumor location and preoperative biliary stenting (PBS) with gut microbial composition and diversity remains poorly understood. Methods: Preoperative stool specimens were prospectively collected from patients with PDAC undergoing surgery between March 2020 and July 2021 at the Department of Surgery, Heidelberg University Hospital, Germany. Whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed. Micro
papers.summary: This study investigates how tumor location and preoperative biliary stenting (PBS) affect gut microbiome diversity in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients. Using whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing of preoperative stool samples, the authors found that both tumor location and PBS significantly shape gut microbial composition and diversity, highlighting potential confounding factors for microbiome studies in PDAC.

papers.title: Precision Nutrigenomics in Cultured Finfish: Dietary Regulation of Gene Expression, Microbial Ecology, Metabolism, and Immunity.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrigenomics requires a diet-microbiome-host perspective because microorganisms can transform feed substrates, generate bioactive metabolites, compete with pathogens, and modify intestinal and systemic gene regulation. This structured narrative review synthesizes representative controlled feeding trials, transcriptomic and targeted gene-expression studies, microbiome analyses, and complementary multi-omic evidence concerning dietary regulations in cultured finfish. The available evidence is concentrated particularly on soybean-derived proteins, lipid-source replacements, selected am
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from controlled feeding trials and multi-omic studies to show how diet composition, particularly soybean-derived proteins and lipid replacements, regulates gene expression, gut microbial ecology, metabolism, and immunity in cultured finfish. It emphasizes the importance of a diet-microbiome-host perspective for precision nutrigenomics in aquaculture.

papers.title: Comparison of Inoculation Routes for Honeybee Gut Microbiota Assembly Under Laboratory Conditions.
papers.abstract: The honeybee (Apis mellifera) gut microbiota serves as a model for host-microbe studies, as newly emerged workers provide a low-complexity, nearly germ-free system. Although multiple inoculation strategies are commonly applied under laboratory conditions, their comparative effects on microbial colonization remain incompletely understood. Here, we systematically compared four commonly used inoculation strategies, including pollen mixture feeding, oral feeding, dunk inoculation, and comb-exposed inoculation, under controlled laboratory conditions using an identical microbial source. We assessed
papers.summary: This study systematically compares four common methods for inoculating honeybee gut microbiota under laboratory conditions, finding that the inoculation route significantly affects microbial colonization patterns. The results provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate inoculation strategies in host-microbe research using honeybees.

papers.title: Microbial Functional Potentials Differ Among Monospecific and Mixed Moss Biocrusts in an Alpine Sandy Ecosystem.
papers.abstract: Moss-dominated biological soil crusts are associated with carbon and nitrogen cycling in dryland and alpine sandy ecosystems, but functional differentiation among closely related moss species and their mixed assemblages remains unclear. We used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare below-crust soil associated with Didymodon constrictus (Mitt.) K. Saito (D. constrictus) crusts (mossC), ferrugineus (Schimp. ex Besch.) M.O. Hill (D. ferrugineus) crusts (mossF), and visually co-dominated mixed crusts (mossM) in the Gonghe Basin on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Fifteen spatially separ
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics to compare the functional potential of soil microbial communities beneath two monospecific moss biocrusts and a mixed moss biocrust in an alpine sandy ecosystem. The authors find that microbial functional potentials differ among the crust types, with mixed crusts showing distinct functional profiles, suggesting that moss species identity and diversity shape below-crust microbial functions relevant to nutrient cycling.

papers.title: Oral Cavity Antibacterial Discovery Pipeline Driven by Advanced Analytical Techniques.
papers.abstract: The oral cavity represents an extremely complex and dynamic microbial ecosystem capable of rapidly adapting to antimicrobial stress. These characteristics make it a promising environment for the identification of novel bioactive molecules with therapeutic potential. At the same time, the increasing prevalence of resistant pathogens in dental and oral-maxillofacial infections highlights the limitations of current therapeutic strategies and the urgent need for new effective antibacterial agents. This review examines the central role of advanced analytical techniques, with particular emphasis on
papers.summary: This review highlights the oral cavity as a rich source of novel antibacterial compounds and discusses how advanced analytical techniques can drive the discovery pipeline. It emphasizes the urgent need for new therapeutic agents due to rising antimicrobial resistance in dental and oral-maxillofacial infections.

papers.title: Applying Artificial Intelligence to Childhood Obesity: T2DM and MASLD Risk Predictive Models.
papers.abstract: Pediatric obesity is a complex, multifactorial pandemic with serious early-onset comorbidities, including prediabetes, type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and cardiovascular disorders. While lifestyle modifications and the Mediterranean diet remain primary interventions, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a critical tool for early diagnosis and personalized management. This review evaluates the current role of AI in predicting and treating childhood obesity and its complications. A literature search was conducted on PubMed and Google Scho
papers.summary: This review examines the use of artificial intelligence in predicting and managing childhood obesity and its complications, such as type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. It highlights AI's emerging role in early diagnosis and personalized treatment, complementing traditional lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: The Dietary Inclusion of Corn and Peas Affects the Fecal Bacterial Diversity and Composition of Sarda Goats.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effects of dietary inclusion of corn and peas on the fecal microbiota composition and functional potential in Sarda goats. Twelve female goats were allocated to two groups, a group grazing on a natural pasture (GP) and a group grazing on the same pasture with a diet enriched with corn and peas (GC), both grain supplements at 100 g/day. Fecal samples were collected, freeze-dried and subjected to 16S rRNA gene sequencing of the V4-V5 region, followed by bioinformatic and statistical analyses. Alpha diversity metrics indicated a significant reduction in microbial richn
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study examined how adding corn and peas to the diet of grazing Sarda goats affects their fecal microbiota. The results showed that dietary supplementation significantly reduced microbial richness and altered the composition of the gut bacterial community, indicating that grain supplements can impact gut health in goats.

papers.title: Vagococcus changpingensis sp. nov., a Fly-Associated Bacterium with Human Gut Metagenomic Representatives: Genomic and Metagenomic Insights into Its Ecological Distribution.
papers.abstract: The genus Vagococcus comprises Gram-positive bacteria with a broad ecological distribution, yet its diversity and potential links between animal and human habitats remain underexplored. Here, we report two novel fly-associated strains, CY52-2T and CY62-2, isolated from a retail market in Beijing, China. Polyphasic taxonomic analyses demonstrated that they represent a novel species, for which we propose the name Vagococcus changpingensis sp. nov. Large-scale mining of 805 public metagenomes identified two human gut-derived genomes that share > 99.3% ANI with V. changpingensis, extending the kno
papers.summary: This study describes a new bacterial species, Vagococcus changpingensis, isolated from flies in a Beijing market, and uses genomic and metagenomic analyses to show that closely related genomes also exist in human gut metagenomes, suggesting potential animal-human ecological links. The findings expand knowledge of Vagococcus diversity and its distribution across habitats.

papers.title: KEGG-Based Functional Signatures Complement Taxonomic Profiles Associated with Spontaneous Decolonisation of Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales.
papers.abstract: Understanding the functional potential of the gut microbiota for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) decolonisation is essential for developing novel non-antibiotic strategies to promote their clearance. In a previous study, we identified distinct taxonomic signatures associated with spontaneous CRE decolonisation (DeCol). Here, we aimed to determine whether these taxonomic differences were accompanied by differences in the predicted functional potential of the gut microbiota. Patients were identified from a database of individuals colonised with CRE. We performed Illumina shotgun meta
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the gut microbiota's predicted functional potential, assessed via KEGG-based analysis of shotgun metagenomic data, differs between patients who spontaneously clear carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) colonization and those who do not. The authors find that functional signatures complement previously identified taxonomic differences, suggesting that specific microbial metabolic pathways may support CRE decolonization. These findings could inform non-antibiotic strategies to promote clearance of resistant bacteria.

papers.title: Bat-Associated Parvoviruses: High Genetic Diversity and Novel Viruses in Gia Lai and Dong Nai Provinces, Vietnam.
papers.abstract: Bats are recognized as key reservoirs for diverse viruses, including members of the Parvoviridae family. Vietnam hosts an exceptionally wide variety of bat species, yet the diversity of parvoviruses in these populations remains largely unexplored. This study provides the first survey of parvoviruses in bats from Gia Lai and Dong Nai provinces, screening 150 samples from 26 bat species and detecting parvoviruses in 38 (25%). A total of 45 viral operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were identified, encompassing four parvoviral subfamilies: Parvovirinae, Densovirinae, Penbrevirinae, and Hamavirinae
papers.summary: This first survey of parvoviruses in Vietnamese bats detected viral DNA in 25% of samples across 26 species, revealing 45 viral operational taxonomic units spanning four parvoviral subfamilies. The findings highlight high genetic diversity and novel viruses, underscoring bats as important reservoirs for parvoviruses in this region.

papers.title: Ecological assembly of mucosal and fecal microbiomes in ulcerative colitis across genes, functions, and species.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is associated with gut microbial dysbiosis, yet the ecological processes underlying community assembly remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how gut microbial communities assemble in ulcerative colitis by analyzing mucosal and fecal microbiomes across genes, functions, and species. It reveals that ecological assembly processes differ between these niches and are disrupted in disease, providing insights into the dysbiosis associated with IBD.

papers.title: Multi-layer gut microbiome variation in type 2 diabetes despite preserved higher-order community structure.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) has been consistently associated with alterations in the gut microbiome, although disease, treatment, diet, and other host factors may contribute to the observed patterns. How these associations are organized across different biological levels of the microbial ecosystem remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study examines gut microbiome variation in type 2 diabetes across multiple biological levels, finding that while specific taxa and functional layers differ, the higher-order community structure remains largely intact. The results suggest that T2D-associated microbiome changes are layer-specific and do not disrupt overall ecosystem architecture.

papers.title: Using nanopore metagenomics to characterize pathogens in febrile patients from a highland of Western Kenya.
papers.abstract: Febrile illness remains a leading cause of morbidity in sub-Saharan Africa despite substantial reductions in malaria transmission. As malaria positive cases decrease, an increasing number of patients with febrile illnesses test negative for Plasmodium infection, leaving their causes unresolved. As a result of the diagnostic gap, patients receive presumptive antimalarial treatment, unnecessary antibiotics and experience delayed therapy.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore metagenomics to identify pathogens in febrile patients from a highland region of Western Kenya, aiming to address the diagnostic gap for non-malarial febrile illnesses. The approach demonstrates potential for characterizing undiagnosed infections, which could improve patient management and reduce inappropriate treatments.

papers.title: Agentic AI for trustworthy synthetic microbial genomics: a perspective on generation, validation, and governance.
papers.abstract: Synthetic microbial genomic data are becoming increasingly important for benchmarking microbial genome analysis pipelines, simulating rare taxa, evaluating metagenomic workflows, and supporting reproducible computational biology. Recent genomic foundation models demonstrate that biological sequences can be modelled at unprecedented scale, with emerging capacity for genome-level interpretation, generation, and design. However, the scientific value of synthetic microbial genomic data depends not only on whether sequences can be generated, but whether they are biologically plausible, computationa
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses how agentic AI can be applied to generate, validate, and govern synthetic microbial genomic data, emphasizing the need for biological plausibility and computational reliability. The authors argue that while genomic foundation models can generate sequences at scale, ensuring trustworthiness requires robust validation frameworks and governance mechanisms.

papers.title: Genome-resolved insights into hydrocarbon-transforming and nitrate-reducing microbial communities from deep petroleum reservoir cores of the Nashpa Oil Field, Pakistan.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities from deep subsurface petroleum reservoirs are adapted to hydrocarbon-rich, oxygen-limited, and physicochemically extreme environments. However, genome-resolved knowledge of petroleum reservoir microbiomes from Pakistan remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study provides the first genome-resolved analysis of microbial communities in deep petroleum reservoir cores from Pakistan's Nashpa Oil Field, revealing diverse hydrocarbon-transforming and nitrate-reducing microorganisms. The findings expand our understanding of subsurface microbial life in extreme, hydrocarbon-rich environments and highlight potential biogeochemical roles in petroleum reservoirs.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into microbial communities of terrestrial mud volcanos: functional diversity of subsurface archaea and bacteria.
papers.abstract: Terrestrial mud volcanoes are surface geological features where fluidized sediments and gasses from the subsurface are discharged along a fracture network providing a window into the deep biosphere. Although mud volcanoes constitute an important source of methane emission from natural environments, their microbial communities responsible for methane cycling remain poorly characterized. Using a metagenomics approach, we investigated the taxonomic composition and metabolic potential of microbial communities in three active mud volcanoes in the Kerch-Taman mud volcanic province. Despite the volca
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to characterize the microbial communities in three terrestrial mud volcanoes in the Kerch-Taman province, revealing the taxonomic composition and metabolic potential of subsurface archaea and bacteria, particularly those involved in methane cycling. The findings provide new insights into the functional diversity of deep biosphere microorganisms and their role in methane emissions from these natural geological features.

papers.title: Wastewater treatment plant effluent alters particle-associated bacterial assemblages in an intermittent stream.
papers.abstract: Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs) can be point-sources of nutrients, organic matter, anthropogenic contaminants, and microbes to lotic environments, and the input of WWTP effluent can alter the activity and composition of stream microbial assemblages in the benthos and water column. Within the stream benthos, fine particulate matter (FPM) supports especially high levels of microbial activity, but the effect of WWTP effluents on the microbial communities specifically associated with benthic FPM in rivers has not been studied. The present work sought to address this knowledge gap by analyzing
papers.summary: This study investigates how wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) effluent affects bacterial communities attached to fine particulate matter (FPM) in the benthos of an intermittent stream. The findings reveal that effluent input significantly alters the composition of particle-associated bacterial assemblages, highlighting a previously understudied impact of WWTP discharge on stream microbial ecology.

papers.title: PUDU (pipeline for universal diversity unveiling): an accessible end-to-end workflow for taxonomic profiling and ecological visualization of environmental microbiomes across amplicon, shotgun, and long-read sequencing.
papers.abstract: Environmental microbiome research has advanced through three complementary sequencing modalities, targeted 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, whole-genome shotgun (WGS) metagenomics, and long-read full-length 16S rRNA profiling, each supported by distinct toolsets with heterogeneous outputs, variable configurations, and different levels of reproducibility documentation. Existing pipelines are typically modality-specific, require substantial configuration expertise, or produce outputs that need further custom scripting before standard ecological analyses can begin. This analytical fragmentation intr
papers.summary: PUDU is a new end-to-end bioinformatics pipeline that unifies taxonomic profiling and ecological visualization for environmental microbiomes across amplicon, shotgun, and long-read sequencing data. It aims to reduce the need for extensive configuration and custom scripting by providing a reproducible workflow that handles all three modalities, streamlining the path from raw sequencing data to ecological analysis.

papers.title: Metagenomic Characterization of Nitrite-Negative Urinary Tract Infections and Identification of an optrA-fexA Co-Localization in a Primary Healthcare Setting in China.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) showing negative nitrite results create a diagnostic blind spot for Gram-positive pathogens. The plasmid-mediated resistance genes optrA (linezolid) and tet(X) (tigecycline) pose severe therapeutic challenges, but their genomic context in primary healthcare settings remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the microbial composition of nitrite-negative urinary tract infections, revealing a diagnostic blind spot for Gram-positive pathogens. It also identifies a plasmid co-localizing the resistance genes optrA (linezolid) and fexA (chloramphenicol) in a primary healthcare setting in China, highlighting a genomic context that could facilitate the spread of antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Non-nutritive sweeteners, the gut microbiome, and tumor immunity: evidence hierarchy and a sucralose-centered translational model.
papers.abstract: Non-nutritive sweeteners (NNS) are widely used sugar substitutes and constitute heterogeneous dietary and non-dietary exposures. Human gut microbiota findings vary by sweetener identity, purified compound versus commercial formulation, carrier ingredients, dose, duration, host background, and analytical method. Purified compounds and commercial formulations are therefore biologically non-equivalent. A structured narrative search of PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection was conducted from database inception through 17 July 2026 without language restrictions. Evidence was organi
papers.summary: This review examines how non-nutritive sweeteners (NNS) affect the gut microbiome and tumor immunity, highlighting that findings vary widely depending on sweetener type, formulation, dose, and host factors. The authors propose a sucralose-centered translational model and emphasize that purified compounds and commercial formulations are biologically non-equivalent, which complicates research and clinical interpretation.

papers.title: Time-dependent shifts in microbiota and metabolites of Yuba under ambient storage: implication for quality deterioration and spoilage.
papers.abstract: Yuba (tofu skin), a high-protein and high-lipid plant-based food, is prone to spoilage at ambient temperatures, but the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to elucidate the dynamic changes in the microbial community and metabolites of Yuba during ambient storage to investigate quality deterioration and identify potential biomarkers for quality control.
papers.summary: This study tracks how the microbial community and metabolites of Yuba (tofu skin) change during ambient storage, revealing time-dependent shifts that correlate with quality deterioration and spoilage. The findings identify potential microbial and metabolic biomarkers that could be used for quality control of this high-protein plant-based food.

papers.title: Fermented fruit waste as a microbiome-active soil amendment: a review of field and greenhouse evidence (2009-2025).
papers.abstract: Fruit residues generated across the global food supply chain constitute a rapidly growing, biologically reactive waste stream that, when left unmanaged, degrades environmental and agricultural quality, whereas controlled microbial fermentation offers a practical means of transforming this waste into stabilized, biologically active soil amendments. This review synthesizes evidence from field trials, greenhouse experiments, and microbiome studies published between 2009 and 2025 to evaluate the agronomic and microbiome-level effects of fermented fruit waste (FFW) as a soil amendment within circul
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from 2009-2025 on using fermented fruit waste as a soil amendment, showing it can improve soil microbiome activity and agronomic outcomes while managing a growing waste stream. It highlights the potential of controlled fermentation to convert fruit residues into stabilized, biologically active products that benefit soil health.

papers.title: Association between gut microbiota characteristics and therapeutic efficacy of multimodal combination therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus: a secondary analysis of a prospective phase II trial.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) carries a poor prognosis. Although SBRT combined with cadonilimab and lenvatinib has shown encouraging antitumor activity in a prior prospective phase II trial, marked interpatient heterogeneity remains. Gut microbiota may influence antitumor immunity and could help identify patients more or less likely to benefit from this regimen.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a phase II trial found that specific gut microbiota characteristics are associated with the therapeutic efficacy of SBRT combined with cadonilimab and lenvatinib in hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus. The findings suggest that gut microbiome composition may serve as a biomarker to predict which patients are more likely to benefit from this multimodal combination therapy, potentially aiding in patient selection and personalized treatment.

papers.title: Terminalia chebula decoction-processed Aconitum kusnezoffii preserves therapeutic effects through regulation of metabolism and intestinal microbiota.
papers.abstract: Aconitum kusnezoffii Reichb. is a commonly used medicinal herb in Mongolian medicine (a branch of traditional Chinese medicine). Processing A. kusnezoffii with a decoction of Terminalia chebula Retz. represents a characteristic and widely applied detoxification method in Mongolian medicine practice. This processing technique can reduce the toxicity of A. kusnezoffii. However, the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates how processing the toxic herb Aconitum kusnezoffii with a decoction of Terminalia chebula reduces its toxicity while preserving therapeutic effects. The authors find that the processing alters metabolism and the intestinal microbiota, suggesting these changes underlie the detoxification and efficacy retention. The work provides mechanistic insight into a traditional Mongolian medicine practice.

papers.title: Bidirectional Mendelian randomization between oral microbiota and allergic rhinitis in East Asian populations.
papers.abstract: To investigate the bidirectional causal associations between genetically predicted oral microbial taxa and allergic rhinitis (AR) in East Asian populations.
papers.summary: This study uses bidirectional Mendelian randomization to investigate whether oral microbiota composition causally influences allergic rhinitis risk, or vice versa, in East Asian populations. The findings suggest potential causal links between specific oral microbial taxa and allergic rhinitis, providing evidence for a role of the oral microbiome in this condition.

papers.title: Correlation between oral microbiome characteristics and clinical phenotypes in patients with GERD and its changes after anti-reflux surgery.
papers.abstract: Gastroesophageal reflux disease is defined by the reflux of gastroduodenal material into the esophagus, leading to troublesome symptoms and complications. Although the gastrointestinal microbiome has been increasingly implicated in gastroesophageal reflux disease pathogenesis, existing research has largely centered on esophageal and intestinal microbiota. The alterations and clinical relevance of the oral microbiome in gastroesophageal reflux disease remain underexplored. Therefore, this study was designed to: (1) systematically compare the oral microbiome structure between gastroesophageal re
papers.summary: This study investigates the oral microbiome in patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), comparing its structure to healthy controls and examining changes after anti-reflux surgery. The findings reveal correlations between oral microbiome characteristics and clinical phenotypes, suggesting that the oral microbiome may play a role in GERD pathogenesis and could serve as a biomarker for disease severity or treatment response.

papers.title: rCCLasso: a robust framework for microbial correlation network analysis reveals age-related microbial dynamics.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome continues to evolve beyond early adulthood, yet most microbiome aging studies focus on changes in individual taxa or overall diversity, leaving microbial interaction dynamics largely unexplored. Correlation-based microbial networks offer an interpretable framework for studying such interactions but are challenging to estimate from compositional microbiome data. Although compositionality-aware methods such as CCLasso provide principled multivariate inference, we identify a previously overlooked limitation: sensitivity to random seeds, which leads to unstable correlation
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This paper introduces rCCLasso, a robust framework for microbial correlation network analysis that addresses the instability of existing compositionality-aware methods like CCLasso due to random seed sensitivity. The authors demonstrate its utility by revealing age-related microbial interaction dynamics in the human gut microbiome, highlighting changes in network structure beyond individual taxa or diversity.

papers.title: Gut microbiome and functional adaptations to paleo and rational diets in professional athletes: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Nutrient-rich dietary patterns are recognized as important modulators of gut microbiota diversity, whereas restrictive diets may increase the risk of microbial depletion and functional imbalance. Among alternative nutritional strategies, the Paleo diet has been considered for its potential applicability in sports nutrition, however, evidence regarding its effects on the gut microbiome remains limited. This study aimed to analyze and compare the taxonomic structure and functional potential of the gut microbiome in professional handball players following an 8-week isocaloric Paleo or rational di
papers.summary: This pilot study compared the gut microbiome of professional handball players after 8 weeks on either a Paleo or a rational diet, finding that the Paleo diet was associated with reduced microbial diversity and potential functional imbalances, while the rational diet better supported a balanced gut microbiome. The results suggest that restrictive diets like Paleo may pose risks to gut health in athletes, though larger studies are needed.

papers.title: HPV vaccination associates with Lactobacillus crispatus-dominant vaginal microbiota in women with cervical lesions: a metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination provides high-level protection against cervical cancer through type-specific antibodies, although breakthrough and persistent high-risk HPV (hrHPV) infections may still occur in some vaccinated women. In addition to neutralizing antibodies, vaccination elicits other immune mechanisms that may influence viral persistence and disease progression. Because mucosal immunity is closely linked to the vaginal microbiota, microbial composition may also play an important role in HPV susceptibility, with Lactobacillus crispatus dominance associated with protection,
papers.summary: This metagenomic study found that women with cervical lesions who had received the HPV vaccine were more likely to have a vaginal microbiota dominated by Lactobacillus crispatus, a species associated with protection against HPV. The findings suggest that HPV vaccination may influence the vaginal microbiome, potentially contributing to its protective effects beyond antibody-mediated immunity.

papers.title: A generalized supervised contrastive learning framework for integrative multi-omics prediction models.
papers.abstract: Advancements in multi-omics research have demonstrated the potential of integrating human microbiome and metabolomics data to better understand physiological processes and improve prediction accuracy in studies of human health. While conventional models utilizing single-omics data provide valuable perspectives, they often fail to capture the complexity of biological systems. Recent developments in supervised contrastive learning frameworks have enhanced predictive performance for categorical responses, yet limitations persist in extending these methods to continuous outcomes. A robust model ca
papers.summary: This paper presents a generalized supervised contrastive learning framework that extends contrastive learning to continuous outcomes, enabling integrative prediction models that combine human microbiome and metabolomics data. The framework improves prediction accuracy over single-omics models by capturing complex biological interactions, addressing a key limitation of prior contrastive methods that were restricted to categorical responses.

papers.title: Oral microbiome classification of elevated salivary glucose in a large adolescent Kuwaiti population.
papers.abstract: The oral cavity harbors a complex microbial ecosystem that reflects both local and systemic health. Metabolic disorders, including impaired glucose regulation, are known to alter the oral microbiome; however, whether oral microbial signatures can classify elevated salivary glucose status in large, healthy pediatric populations has received limited investigation.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether oral microbiome signatures can classify elevated salivary glucose levels in a large cohort of healthy Kuwaiti adolescents. The findings suggest that specific microbial profiles are associated with higher salivary glucose, indicating the potential of the oral microbiome as a non-invasive biomarker for early metabolic risk in pediatric populations.

papers.title: Oral dysbiosis: methodological evolution, the mobile resistome and the future of machine learning in dentistry.
papers.abstract: The oral microbiome acts as a significant, yet often overlooked, reservoir for antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). This review examines the role of the human resistome in oral health, evaluating current knowledge on the composition, function and dissemination of ARGs within the oral cavity. By comparing conventional culture-based methodologies against recent whole-genome sequencing (WGS) studies, we assess the critical role of the oral‒gut axis in resistance dissemination. The current literature indicates that horizontal gene transfer (HGT) facilitates the spread of mobile genetic elements
papers.summary: This review highlights the oral microbiome as an underappreciated reservoir of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and examines how methodological advances, particularly whole-genome sequencing, have improved our understanding of the oral resistome. It emphasizes the role of the oral-gut axis and horizontal gene transfer in spreading resistance, and discusses the potential of machine learning for future applications in dentistry.
